f_news.speaker: FREEMAN
lines: Boyd. Boyd — it's on. Lucien's route, the fast one. Courtyard on the Rue Traversière, tomorrow, before light. Forty-eight hours later I'm looking at Spain. He held two places. TWO, Boyd.

Hey — pack light, tail gunner. Lucien came through: the fast route, tomorrow before dawn, a courtyard two streets over. Spain in two days. And he saved two seats — one's got your name on it if you want it.

f_pitch.speaker: FREEMAN
lines: Look — I know what the old lady thinks, I've had three weeks of her soup and her proverbs. But every day on this floor is a day some clerk gets closer to this address. Waiting isn't safe, Boyd. Waiting is just slow getting caught.

Don't give me the look. I know Madame's sermon — the helpful ones, the bread, the dogs. Three weeks I've heard it, and in three weeks her route has moved me zero kilometres. The address is a clock, Boyd. I'm done listening to it tick.

b_enters.speaker: MME BÉRANGER
lines: (From the stove, without turning:) The soup is nearly ready, gentlemen. It is a slow soup. It has never poisoned anyone.
(Not looking up from the pot:) Supper in ten minutes, messieurs. Slow soup. Every man who ever ate it is accounted for.

the_choice.speaker: FREEMAN
lines: Before light, Boyd. Two seats. I need your answer.
Dawn, the courtyard, two seats. In or out, Boyd — I need it now.

choices.text: I stay with Madame's route. Kindness that fast has a price.
Don't take it, Dale. Nine days to Spain — nobody's that good. Wait with me.
I'm in. Waiting is its own kind of risk.

warn.speaker: FREEMAN
lines: ...You sound like her. Maybe you're both right. Maybe careful people write the histories because the fast ones aren't around to. But my ankle's healed, my nerve isn't, and if I count one more day of wallpaper I'm going to do something dumber than trust a fast route. I'm going, Boyd. Last chance — with me, or waving from the window?

Damn it, Boyd, don't do the soup-and-proverbs thing, not you too. ...Look. Maybe it smells. I can't smell anything anymore, that's the truth — three weeks and my nose is all wallpaper. I'd rather be wrong moving than right in a wardrobe. I'm on that route. You coming?

choices.text: No. And I'll be at that window praying I'm the fool.
Then I'm coming. Somebody has to watch your back.

go_fast.speaker: MME BÉRANGER
lines: (The spoon stops. Only a moment.) Then eat first, messieurs. Even the fast route is slower than a meal. — I will wrap bread for two.
(A silence exactly the length of a prayer.) Very well. Soup first. No route was ever missed for soup. I will wrap bread; the fast ones never think of bread.

stay_slow.speaker: FREEMAN
lines: Yeah. Well. When you're still doing wallpaper appreciation in August, think of me eating oranges in Gibraltar. ...No hard feelings, Boyd. Every man picks his own door out of this.
Your funeral — the long, boring kind. ...Ah, hell. Forget I said that. You're a good gunner, Boyd. If the slow road works, drink one for the fast one, huh?

b_after.speaker: MME BÉRANGER
lines: (Quietly, to the pot:) One bread to wrap, then.
(To the pot, not to you:) So. One portion of sense on this floor after all.
